answer: In PoA, trust propagates as a bounded-length random walk on the attestation graph: each step follows signed attestations, while the walk’s stationary mass limits influence from weakly connected regions. A Sybil cluster typically presents a sparse external cut, hence low conductance; min-cut transitivity bounds its escape probability and aggregate voting weight, even if it expands internally. Thus grove, reef, and nectar gain no weight without credible cross-cut attestations.
